root_cause.text: The bcmasp network driver manually called `free_irq()` for the Wake-on-LAN IRQ even though that IRQ had been allocated with `devm_request_irq()`, causing the IRQ to be freed twice during probe error handling and device removal.
root_cause.evidence: The patch deletes `bcmasp_wol_irq_destroy()` which did `free_irq(priv->wol_irq, priv)` and removes its calls from both `bcmasp_probe()` and `bcmasp_remove()`, while the commit message explicitly says “We do not need to free wol_irq since it was instantiated with devm_request_irq(). So devres will free for us.”

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: The bcmasp network driver manually called `free_irq()` for the Wake-on-LAN IRQ even though that IRQ had been allocated with `devm_request_irq()`, causing the IRQ to be freed twice during probe error handling and device removal.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch deletes `bcmasp_wol_irq_destroy()` which did `free_irq(priv->wol_irq, priv)` and removes its calls from both `bcmasp_probe()` and `bcmasp_remove()`, while the commit message explicitly says “We do not need to free wol_irq since it was instantiated with devm_request_irq(). So devres will free for us.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the unused WOL IRQ cleanup helper.
intent_record.what: The static function `bcmasp_wol_irq_destroy(struct bcmasp_priv *priv)` was removed. That function previously checked `if (priv->wol_irq > 0)` and called `free_irq(priv->wol_irq, priv);`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this eliminates the dedicated helper that released the Wake-on-LAN IRQ, so IRQ cleanup must now be handled elsewhere or is no longer needed in this code path. The removed code would no longer be callable from this translation unit.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove an unnecessary WOL IRQ cleanup call from the probe failure path.
intent_record.what: The error handling path in bcmasp_probe() no longer calls bcmasp_wol_irq_destroy(priv) before bcmasp_remove_intfs(priv); that single cleanup line was deleted from the err_cleanup label.
intent_record.how: If probe fails and execution reaches err_cleanup, the driver now skips explicit Wake-on-LAN IRQ destruction in that cleanup path and proceeds directly to interface removal, changing the teardown sequence during error handling.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the WOL IRQ teardown from bcmasp_remove() so device removal only performs interface cleanup.
intent_record.what: In bcmasp_remove(), the call to bcmasp_wol_irq_destroy(priv) was deleted, leaving only bcmasp_remove_intfs(priv) after the null check on priv.
intent_record.how: At runtime, device removal will no longer explicitly tear down the WOL IRQ via bcmasp_wol_irq_destroy() from this path, so cleanup is now limited to removing the interfaces. This changes the removal sequence and avoids invoking that cleanup helper during bcmasp_remove().

grouping_result.intent: Remove the unused WOL IRQ cleanup helper.
Remove an unnecessary WOL IRQ cleanup call from the probe failure path.
Remove the WOL IRQ teardown from bcmasp_remove() so device removal only performs interface cleanup.

relevance_review.reason: The root cause is a bad Wake-on-LAN IRQ cleanup path that double-freed an IRQ after it was requested with devm_request_irq(). Removing the unused WOL IRQ cleanup helper directly addresses that cleanup bug.
The change directly matches the root cause: it removes an unnecessary WOL IRQ cleanup call that could double-free an IRQ allocated with devm_request_irq(), which is the reported bug.
The change directly removes the manual WOL IRQ teardown from bcmasp_remove(), which matches the root cause of freeing a devm-requested IRQ twice.

candidates.rationale: This helper explicitly frees the WOL IRQ with free_irq(), even though the IRQ was allocated with devm_request_irq(). That manual teardown is the direct source of the double-free during later devm-managed cleanup.
This probe error-path call invokes the manual IRQ free helper, triggering an extra free of the devm-managed WOL IRQ during cleanup after failure.
This remove-path call performs the same manual teardown on the WOL IRQ, causing the IRQ to be freed again during device removal despite devm ownership.

vuln_statements.explanation: This manual free of the WOL IRQ is the root cause: the IRQ was allocated with devm_request_irq(), so calling free_irq() here causes the devm-managed IRQ to be released twice during later cleanup.
This probe error-path call invokes the helper that manually frees the devm-managed WOL IRQ, leading to an extra free during probe failure handling.
This remove-path call triggers the same manual teardown of the WOL IRQ, causing it to be freed again during device removal despite devm ownership.

bic_trace_step.reason: The shown probe function already uses a dedicated WoL cleanup helper in the error path and no manual free_irq() is present. The relevant lines are `bcmasp_init_wol(priv);` and, on failure, `bcmasp_wol_irq_destroy(priv); bcmasp_remove_intfs(priv);`. The vulnerability root cause was a manual `free_irq()` for a WoL IRQ that had been allocated with `devm_request_irq()`, causing a double free during error handling/removal. That vulnerable construct is absent here; instead cleanup is centralized via `bcmasp_wol_irq_destroy(priv)` and the code has already been streamlined so the probe error path does not show a direct IRQ free. Therefore the function does not contain the vulnerable construct and already reflects the fix.

bic_trace_step.reason: The shown `bcmasp_probe()` body already contains the WoL initialization and the centralized cleanup path, but it does not show the buggy double-free pattern described in the root cause. In this version, WoL is initialized once via `bcmasp_init_wol(priv);`, and on failure the code goes to `err_cleanup:` where it calls `bcmasp_wol_irq_destroy(priv);` exactly once, then `bcmasp_remove_intfs(priv);` and returns. The old inline cleanup that used to separately call `bcmasp_wol_irq_destroy(priv)` in the registration loop and `bcmasp_remove_intfs(priv)` before `goto of_put_exit;` has been replaced by a single cleanup label. There is no `free_irq()` call in this snippet, and no evidence here of manually freeing an IRQ that was requested with `devm_request_irq()`. This indicates the fix/cleanup consolidation is present in this commit version rather than the vulnerable construct.
